- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (e.g., +1.00 or +0.25 in recent days) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bearish (e.g., -1.00 or 0.00 in recent days) — raise forecast low by 5–10%.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — if last 3–5 days show sharp upward movement, cap forecast peak at 1–2% below prior high.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00/0.20), model should not overfit recent volatility — use 3–5 day moving average for smoothing.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid “over-optimistic” tail behavior — if forecast ends with 3+ consecutive rising days, check for horizon mismatch; reduce final 3–5 days by 2–5% if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- If sentiment turns sharply bullish after a dip, model should not overcorrect — allow 1–2 day lag in price reaction to sentiment shift.
